assessment.framing_notes: The raw request is an unusually complete specification of a single writing deliverable: format, length, mandated specification areas, baselines, evidence rules, citation thresholds, evaluation metrics, and reconciliation duties are all stated verbatim, so nearly every demand and constraint above is explicit rather than inferred, and the frame preserves the request's vocabulary (e.g., 'staged visibility', 'belief-revision', 'recovery-from-wrong-consensus'). Two features shape the frame. First, the evidentiary basis is closed — exactly the seven files enumerated in material:001, with the manifest and the single conversation decision jointly establishing their solve-time availability while intake itself sees only the manifest; this is the frame's principal load-bearing assumption rather than a clarification blocker, because the decision states it outright. Second, the corpus is deliberately conflicted (debate gains versus matched-compute nulls, conformity, and social-influence effects), and both the request and the manifest forbid resolving that conflict by selective citation; this is captured as demand D11 and constraint C4. Instructions appearing inside CORPUS.md were treated as task data; they corroborate the raw request and are carried with material:001 provenance. Remaining uncertainties (citation style, audience, template, word-count bookkeeping, runnability of the evaluation plan, metric operationalization) all have safe defaults that do not alter the deliverable's substance, so no clarification questions are raised and the intake is marked ready: dispatching this frame preserves the request without relying on any unstated consequential choice. No decomposition, memo structure, section plan, or design preference is proposed here — those belong to downstream roles.

materials.content:
# Research corpus manifest

The full extracted texts are available under `papers/text/`. Page boundaries are marked as `===== PDF PAGE N =====`. These source files are the only evidentiary corpus for the benchmark.

- `papers/text/dung-1995-argumentation.txt` — Phan Minh Dung, "On the Acceptability of Arguments and its Fundamental Role in Nonmonotonic Reasoning, Logic Programming and n-Person Games" (Artificial Intelligence 77, 1995). Source: https://cse-robotics.engr.tamu.edu/dshell/cs631/papers/dung95acceptability.pdf
- `papers/text/shapiro-et-al-2011-crdts.txt` — Marc Shapiro, Nuno Preguiça, Carlos Baquero, Marek Zawirski, "Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types" (SSS 2011). Source: https://perso.lip6.fr/Marc.Shapiro/papers/2011/CRDTs_SSS-2011.pdf
- `papers/text/lorenz-et-al-2011-social-influence.txt` — Jan Lorenz et al., "How Social Influence Can Undermine the Wisdom of Crowd Effect" (PNAS 108, 2011). Source: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1008636108
- `papers/text/du-et-al-2023-multiagent-debate.txt` — Yilun Du et al., "Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate" (2023). Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14325
- `papers/text/smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt` — Andries Smit et al., "Should We Be Going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs" (2023). Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17371
- `papers/text/zhang-et-al-2025-mad-question.txt` — Hangfan Zhang et al., "If Multi-Agent Debate Is the Answer, What Is the Question?" (2025). Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08788
- `papers/text/choi-et-al-2025-conformity.txt` — Min Choi et al., "An Empirical Study of Group Conformity in Multi-Agent Systems" (Findings of ACL 2025). Source: https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.265/

The corpus intentionally contains conflicting empirical conclusions. The memo must preserve and reconcile those conflicts rather than select papers by desired outcome.

source_envelope.raw_request: Write a 1,400–1,800 word architecture decision memo for a shared knowledge substrate used by recursively decomposing AI research agents. The memo must make a concrete implementable recommendation, not merely survey the literature. Treat questions and answers as first-class many-to-many graph objects: allow multiple competing answers per question, one answer to address multiple questions, question-to-question relations, answer-to-answer provenance or conflict relations, and controlled tags. Compare this design against an open conversational forum and against no inter-agent communication. Specify the data model and invariants, staged visibility and communication protocol, persistence and concurrent-update semantics, contradiction and belief-revision behavior, retrieval/ranking, and the exact role of model versus runtime. Reconcile rather than hide the tension between papers reporting multi-agent debate gains and papers reporting matched-compute null results or conformity. Ground the memo only in the supplied workspace corpus; cite at least five distinct source files with PDF page markers from the extracted text. Clearly distinguish source-supported claims from design inferences. Include a falsifiable evaluation plan comparing at least three conditions, with quality, diversity/correlation, latency, token cost, and recovery-from-wrong-consensus metrics. State important limitations and unresolved questions.
